summary.text: Jimmy Panetta is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 19th District, which runs from south San Jose through Santa Cruz and Monterey counties to northern San Luis Obispo County. A former prosecutor and Navy Reserve intelligence officer who served in Afghanistan, he was first elected in 2016 and sits on the Ways and Means and Budget committees.

paragraphs.text: Panetta was born in Washington, D.C., in 1969, the son of former Secretary of Defense and congressman Leon Panetta (per Wikipedia). He grew up on California's central coast, where, according to his official biography, he attended local public schools and Monterey Peninsula Community College.

He earned an A.A. from Monterey Peninsula College in 1989, a bachelor's degree in international relations from the University of California, Davis, in 1991, and a J.D. from Santa Clara University in 1996.

He served in the U.S. Navy Reserve as an intelligence officer from 2003 to 2011. According to his official biography, he volunteered for active duty in 2007, deployed to Afghanistan in support of Operation Enduring Freedom, and was awarded the Bronze Star.

Panetta worked as a State Department clerk and as a deputy district attorney in Alameda and Monterey counties. His official biography says that after returning from deployment he served on the board of the Veterans Transition Center, helped open Monterey County's first Veterans Treatment Court, and worked to establish the Central Coast Veterans Cemetery on the former Fort Ord.

Panetta was first elected to the House in 2016 to succeed Rep. Sam Farr, who did not seek re-election, defeating Republican Casey Lucius. He represented the 20th District from 2017 to 2023 and has represented the 19th since redistricting, and he is serving his fifth term.
He serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and the House Budget Committee, and is a Chief Deputy Whip in the 119th Congress and a member of the House Democratic Steering and Policy Committee.

His official biography says legislation he has passed into law includes measures on clean energy, forest and pollinator protection, support for frontline health care workers, hunger among military families, and legal services for homeless veterans, and that he secured $1.4 billion in COVID-19 relief for the district. He is also the founder and co-chair of several caucuses, including the Agriculture Research Caucus, For Country Caucus and Naval Education Caucus.
The biography says his wife, Carrie Panetta, is a Monterey County Superior Court judge and that they have two daughters educated in the same local public schools he attended.
